title: Private Wave Manager and Compatibility Fence for Orchestrated Migrations
creator: Ava Patel
description: Summary: Build a 'Wave Manager' and accompanying 'Compatibility Fence' that together orchestrate staged upgrades for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The Wave Manager drives canary -> staggered waves -> full rollout flows for control-plane and agent components, while the Compatibility Fence enforces preflight compatibility checks, schema migration gate logic, and fast automated rollback triggers. Goals: minimize customer downtime, make DB/schema migrations safe and reversible, provide deterministic gating for LTS channels, and expose operational controls for customers and SREs.
details: Background and motivation: Private customers run heterogeneous clusters with pinned LTS channels and strict maintenance windows. Existing migration tooling covers basic sequencing but lacks an integrated concept of waves with automatic rollback based on health signals, and it does not centralize compatibility assertions (binary version matrix, schema compatibility, agent/connector contract checks). This ticket implements the control-plane actor that coordinates waves and the lightweight compatibility fence that runs prior to and during each wave.
approach: 1) Wave Manager: implement a stateful controller in the private control plane that accepts a rollout manifest (targets, wave size, pause windows, rollback policy). The controller will: create canary cohorts, execute preflight jobs, monitor telemetry (ping, pod readiness, API perf, API error rate, kv cache hit rate), and proceed/abort waves based on configured SLAs. 2) Compatibility Fence: a sidecarless tool run as a job that validates version matrix, on-disk schema checksums, KMS/HSM reachability, and a DB migration dry-run. It publishes a signed artifact (compatibility token) consumed by the Wave Manager. 3) Migration choreography: provide connectors for online schema migrations (chunked, idempotent operations), drift detection and quiesce/unquiesce hooks for stateful services, and an explicit migration plan artifact that can be reheated for dry-runs. 4) Safety nets: full rollback plan including automatic LTS-pin reversion, orchestration of agent rollback on secondaries, and a staged data backfill step for rehydrate scenarios.
tradeoffs: - Complexity vs safety: Wave Manager introduces orchestration complexity and needs strong testing but reduces manual error and MTTR. - Telemetry sensitivity: conservative gates reduce rollout velocity. We will expose gate thresholds as config to customers. - DB migrations: prefer online, chunked patterns; sometimes a blocking migration will be unavoidable for data model changes—those will require maintenance windows and manual approval.
runbook_and_testing: - End-to-end dry-run harness that spins up a synthetic VPC cluster (local-aws-sim environment) and runs a full canary-to-rollout flow using a test model image. - Integration tests: compatibility fence vs example known-good/backwards-incompatible agent builds. - Load tests for gating signals (error-rate and latency thresholds). - Chaos scenarios: network partition, partial agent upgrades, and leader failover. - Operator CLI for manual pause/resume/force-rollback and a 'simulate' mode that only writes expected plan without executing.
operational_contracts: - Gate criteria must be auditable and logged: timestamped events, who/what triggered progression. - Must emit a signed rollout manifest per-wave for audit and supportability. - Telemetry exported to Console: per-wave cost/latency breakdown, tokens consumed, and rollback reasons. - Provide a 'compatibility report' artifact stored with the release record.
acceptance_criteria: Wave Manager can run a canary cohort and automatically roll forward to a 50% wave given healthy signals.
Compatibility Fence produces a signed compatibility token after validating binaries, schema checksums, and KMS reachability.
A failed gate triggers immediate rollback steps and posts clear actionable reasons to the rollout timeline and incident channel.
End-to-end dry-run produces deterministic results and matches the 'simulate' mode output for at least 95% of runs.
Documentation: runbook + customer-facing guide for configuring waves and thresholds in Console are published prior to release.
Security review completed and KMS/HSM integration validated by Security team.

notes: Design decision: compatibility fence will be client-initiated via preflight token request to reduce control-plane blast radius.
We will support a graceful degradation policy where older agents are served by compatible model variants until they upgrade (runtime routing fallback).
Consider adding a post-rollout A/B evaluation job to detect quality regressions tied to model quantization or kernel changes.
